lines.trans: The CEO is ruthless for booking twenty-two events in one week, and you are just as tough for enduring it.
What is the Big Show?
It is a special at KBS, and they say the co-director is Music Bank producer Tak Ye-jin.
Whenever they put on a big special, assistant directors get drafted from all the other teams too.

words.gloss: it works like that, you know

lines.trans: Then might the assistant directors from the 2 Days & 1 Night team come over too?
Oh, you are worried about that umbrella producer—I will strongly demand they keep him far away!
Whenever I say something, just listen to my words exactly as I say them.
Stop trying to dig up some hidden meaning behind them.
Last time you were the one who told me to read between the lines!
That is because you keep reading it wrong—do not read between the lines!

meanings.note: Interrogative or indefinite pronoun; often shortened to 뭐 in casual speech.

examples.trans: What is your favorite food?
What can I help you with?

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: It is a special at KBS, and they say the co-director is Music Bank producer Tak Ye-jin.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.note: describes how things typically work
refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.
It really is is loud, so compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is is loud, so and nice.

meanings.note: common in TV/radio programming and magazines

examples.trans: There is a special broadcast tonight.
I watched the Lunar New Year special program.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: 르-irregular adjective; conjugates as 달라요 in polite present.
In its adnominal form 다른, modifies a following noun to mean 'other' or 'another'.

examples.trans: Do you have any other questions?
Our thoughts are different from each other.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 원래 큰 특집 할 땐 다른 팀에서 조연출이며 다 차출되고 그러잖아.
examples.trans: Whenever they put on a big special, assistant directors get drafted from all the other teams too.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!
Did you hear about this 1 night?
I was busy today because of 1 night.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

meanings.note: Sino-Korean term.

examples.trans: Since it's raining, please use an umbrella.
I lost my umbrella.

meanings.note: Usually followed by -e to mean 'because of'.

examples.trans: I was late because of the rain.
It's because of you.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 술은 정신력이거든요, 제가 정신력이 강해서 기본적으로 잘 취하지를 않고요.
examples.trans: Drinking is all about willpower—my willpower is strong, so basically I hardly ever get drunk.
This expression comes from 'because it is strong'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 그 우산 피디 때문에 그러는구나, 강하게 요구할게 절대 못 오게 해달라고!
examples.trans: Oh, you are worried about that umbrella producer—I will strongly demand they keep him far away!
This expression comes from 'I will demand'.

examples.text: 신디에겐 절대 비밀로 할게요. 걱정 마세요.
examples.trans: I will keep it an absolute secret from Cindy. Don't worry.

examples.text: 절대 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (absolutely), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.note: Placed directly before a noun in questions

examples.trans: What kind of music are you listening to right now?

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.

examples.trans: I just asked out of curiosity.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.

I told you last time.
What did you do last weekend?

examples.trans: I want to read right now.

examples.text: 자꾸 어디 넘어지고 또 칠칠맞게 뭐 하다 다쳤냐?

examples.text: 걱정은 하지, 늘. 근데 왜 백승찬을 집에 자꾸 들이냐?

examples.text: 자꾸 잘못 읽으니까 그렇지, 읽지 마!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
